layout_dets.text: Abstract. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) has demonstrated re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: markable zero-shot capability and flexible geometric prompting in gen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eral image segmentation. However, it often struggles in domains that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are either sparsely represented or lie outside its training distribution,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as aerial, medical, and non-RGB images. Recent efforts have pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dominantly focused on adapting SAM to these domains using fully su-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pervised methods, which necessitate large amounts of annotated train-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing data and pose practical challenges in data collection. This paper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presents CAT-SAM, a ConditionAl Tuning network that explores few-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shot adaptation of SAM toward various challenging downstream domains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a data-efficient manner. The core design is a prompt bridge struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture that enables decoder-conditioned joint tuning of the heavyweight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image encoder and the lightweight mask decoder. The bridging maps the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain-specific features of the mask decoder to the image encoder, fos-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tering synergic adaptation of both components with mutual benefits with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: few-shot target samples only, ultimately leading to superior segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in various downstream tasks. We develop two CAT-SAM variants that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adopt two tuning strategies for the image encoder: one injecting learn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: able prompt tokens in the input space and the other inserting lightweight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adapter networks. Extensive experiments over 11 downstream tasks show

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that CAT-SAM achieves superior segmentation consistently even under

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the very challenging one-shot adaptation setup.

layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Accurate image segmentation is a fundamental computer vision task that plays a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pivotal role in various applications such as robotics, autonomous driving, health-

layout_dets.text: care, earth observation, etc. The recently developed Segment Anything Model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (SAM) [23], trained with 1.1 billion masks, has emerged as a momentous leap for-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ward in image segmentation. By taking geometric prompts with points, boxes, or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: masks as input, SAM demonstrates remarkable zero-shot capability for general

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation, as well as great potential for fine-grained mask segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion in different downstream tasks across a variety of contexts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On the other hand, SAM often fails to generate high-quality predictions when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dealing with domains that are either sparsely represented or lie outside its train-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing distribution [5, 19], such as challenging RGB images including aerial, medical,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and intricate structural images, as well as non-RGB images like X-ray, Sonar,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images, etc. This greatly undermines the ver-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satility and applicability of SAM as a foundational segmentation model while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: handling various downstream tasks. Several studies attempted to address this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: issue by fine-tuning SAM with a large number of target samples with mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations [21, 30]. However, they require extensive masked images for each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specialized field, posing a formidable task with poor scalability. How to effec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively adapt SAM toward various downstream tasks in a data-efficient manner

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has become an essential challenge in the segmentation field.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We exploit few-shot target samples for effective and efficient adaptation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM toward various downstream tasks. Inspired by the recent advancements in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameter-efficient tuning for foundation models [1,13], we freeze the entire SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and lightly expand its image encoder and mask decoder with a tiny amount of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learnable parameters. This expansion preserves SAM's zero-shot capabilities and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flexibility while capturing domain-specific features that are essential for the seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation of downstream data. However, SAM's image encoder is much larger

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than its mask decoder, which directly leads to tuning imbalance and further sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimal adaptation, especially under the limited supervision of few-shot target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: samples.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To address this challenge, we design CAT-SAM, a novel ConditionAl Tuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network for effective and data-efficient adaptation of SAM. The key idea is to ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAT-SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ploit the lightweight decoder tuning to guide the heavyweight encoder tuning and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formulate decoder-conditioned joint tuning of both as depicted in Fig. 1. To this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: end, we design a prompt bridge structure that maps the domain-specific features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the mask decoder to the image encoder. With the collaboration between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two partners, CAT-SAM enables synergistic adaptation of both which mitigates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the tuning imbalance and improves the few-shot SAM adaptation effectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In addition, the prompt bridge can be seamlessly embedded into two represen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tative tuning approaches, including prompt tuning [20, 25, 27] that introduces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learnable prompt tokens into the input space and adapters [15, 29, 37, 38] that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leverage lightweight adaptive networks. This directly leads to two CAT-SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variants, namely, CAT-SAM-T and CAT-SAM-A. Extensive evaluations over 11

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diverse and challenging downstream tasks show that both variants achieve su-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perior adaptation and segmentation with few-shot target samples only.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The major contributions of this work can be summarized in three aspects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: First, we propose CAT-SAM, a conditional tuning network that enables effective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and data-efficient adaptation of SAM toward various challenging downstream do-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mains. We design prompt bridge within CAT-SAM, a decoder-conditioned joint

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tuning structure that enables synergistic and data-efficient adaptation of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heavyweight image encoder and the lightweight mask decoder effectively. Sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ond, we develop two CAT-SAM variants by embedding the prompt bridge into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two representative tuning strategies, one introducing learnable prompt tokens in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the input space and the other inserting lightweight adapter networks. Third, ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tensive experiments over 11 diverse segmentation datasets show that CAT-SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieves superior image segmentation consistently even under the challenging

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one-shot setup.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Parameter-Efficient Tuning for foundation models has become increasingly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crucial due to the over-size model parameters and costly one-task-one-model de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ployment. One popular approach involves updating only the newly added learn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: able parameters while keeping the model backbone frozen. These lightweight pa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rameters are often introduced in two ways: 1) as prompt tuning [12,20,22,58] by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adding learnable tokens to input tokens at transformer layers, 2) as adapters [11,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 29, 37, 38, 49] by integrating learnable lightweight sub-networks into transformer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers. However, prior visual studies primarily focus on adapting single backbone

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modules [3, 20, 29] or dual encoder backbones for vision-language tasks [22, 57],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are suboptimal tuning solutions while applying to SAM due to its particu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lar architecture of a heavyweight image encoder and a lightweight mask decoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In contrast, we explore a novel conditional joint tuning strategy tailored to SAM,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which facilitates its adaptation even with limited downstream data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM for Downstream Tasks. The release of SAM has spurred several sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sequent studies. Some concentrate on expanding semantic recognition capabil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ities [24, 26, 43, 50, 54], while others aim to create more lightweight SAM vari-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ants [48, 52, 55] for faster computations. Several studies explore SAM's adapta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Xiao and W. Xuan et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion in underperforming downstream scenarios, primarily by directly fine-tuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM's mask decoder [4,8,30,41,46, 53], which can severely degrade SAM's zero-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shot capabilities. The recent HQ-SAM [21] freezes the entire pre-trained SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and prompt-tunes the mask decoder with a new mask head for adaptive mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prediction. However, these adaptation studies rely on large target datasets with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a considerable number of annotated images, which are often costly to collect. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contrast, our CAT-SAM achieves superior adaptation with only few-shot target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: samples, significantly reducing adaptation costs and expanding the applicability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of SAM as a visual foundation model.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 Preliminaries of SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM [23] handles each image with three key modules: a heavyweight image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder (i.e., ViT [9] as the backbone) that extracts image embeddings, a prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder that encodes the geometric prompts (i.e., points, a box, or a coarse mask)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to generate prompt embeddings, and a lightweight mask decoder that combines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the two types of embeddings to predict segmentation masks. The released SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model is trained on a super large-scale SA-1B dataset, which consists of over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 11 million images as well as 1.1 billion automatically generated masks. SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has demonstrated remarkable zero-shot capability while dealing with various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conventional natural images, as well as superb flexibility in accepting various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: geometric prompt inputs. On the other hand, it often struggles while facing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenging downstream domains that are often sparse or falling outside of its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training data distribution, such as RGB domains of aerial, medical, and intricate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structural images, as well as non-RGB domains of X-ray, SAR, and Sonar images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: More details about SAM are presented in [23].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 CAT-SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This subsection introduces CAT-SAM, a ConditionAl Tuning network that is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designed for adapting SAM toward various under-performed downstream data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The objective is to adapt SAM efficiently with only few-shot annotated target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images, meanwhile preserving SAM's powerful zero-shot capability and geomet-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ric prompting flexibility

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAT-SAM freezes the entire SAM and facilitates the simultaneous tuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of SAM's image encoder and mask decoder to capture representative informa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion from few-shot target samples for effective adaptation of SAM. However, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: critical issue with simultaneous tuning arises from the clear imbalance between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the heavyweight image encoder (308.3 M parameters for ViT-L [9]) and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lightweight mask decoder (4.1 M), which often leads to sub-optimal adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while only few-shot target samples are available. To tackle this challenge, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: design decoder-conditioned joint tuning, a novel tuning strategy that mitigates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the imbalance by establishing a linkage between the encoding tuning and the de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coding tuning. Specifically, we design prompt bridge—a lightweight network that

layout_dets.text: 3.3 Training and Inference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During training, we feed target samples together with geometric prompts into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAT-SAM to generate CAT-SAM masks, under the supervision of ground-truth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: masks as well as a linear combination of BCE loss and dice loss [31]. We freeze

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pre-trained SAM parameters and update solely the parameters that are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduced in the above-described tuning modules. Note we train CAT-SAM with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a mixture of sampled geometric prompts, including bounding boxes, randomly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selected points, and coarse masks. In addition, we create degraded coarse masks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by introducing random Gaussian noise in the boundary regions of the ground-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: truth masks as in [21]. Further training details can be found in Section 4.1 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the appendix.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During the inference phase, the input image is fed into SAM's image encoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: along with the integrated prompt tokens in CAT-SAM-T or adapters in CAT-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM-A, to generate adaptive image embeddings. These embeddings, combined

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the prompt tokens from SAM's prompt encoder, serve as input to the mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder. Subsequently, the updated CAT-token and associated MLP are utilized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the target mask prediction. Lastly, we up-sample the mask to the original

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution to produce the final output.

layout_dets.text: 5 Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We introduce CAT-SAM, a conditional tuning network tailored for few-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adaptation of SAM. We propose decoder-conditional joint tuning to mitigate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the tuning imbalance between SAM's heavyweight image encoder and lightweight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask decoder and facilitate efficient SAM adaptation. To achieve this, we design

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the prompt bridge structures, enabling interaction when tuning these two net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work modules. We develop two CAT-SAM variants by integrating the prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bridge with two representative tuning strategies including prompt tuning and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adapter. Our comprehensive evaluation across diverse scenarios and tasks on 11

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation datasets underscores the superior domain adaptive efficiency of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both CAT-SAM variants, even in the extremely challenging one-shot scenario.
